item.title: Five dead and 86 missing as 'heartbreaking' fire breaks out on Philippines ferry
item.description:
Multiple search and rescue vessels deployed after blaze off Palawan island leaves at least five dead, says coast guard A large-scale ⁠search and rescue operation is under way off the western Philippine island of Palawan on Thursday after a passenger ferry caught fire, killing five people and leaving ⁠scores of passengers missing. The Philippine coast guard said multiple vessels and other assets were searching for survivors as rescue teams used drift-modelling tools ⁠to identify areas where people may have been carried by currents. item.title: Spain’s spy agency warned of mass crossings into Ceuta before border crisis
item.description:
The EU on Wednesday said it was granting Spain 115 million euros ($130 million) in emergency aid to help bolster border security and assist returns after the massive migrant rush into the north African exclave. More than 70,000 migrants crossed into Spanish territory from Morocco on July 30 and 31 in an unprecedented rush that left scores dead, most by drowning as they tried to swim around a breakwater. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Madrid.

item.title: Missouri’s voting maps saga reaches supreme court after conflicting rulings
item.description:
Appeal against federal panel’s approval of Trump-backed maps is latest move in legal back-and-forth spanning four courts A high-stakes legal battle over Missouri’s congressional map returned on Wednesday to the US supreme court, after a series of conflicting decisions threw the state’s elections into turmoil less than two months before the November midterm elections. On Wednesday, a federal appeals court panel declined to block a ruling ordering Missouri to use the newly drawn congressional lines backed by Donald Trump to give Republicans an edge in the midterms elections. Opponents of the state’s redistricted map immediately filed an appeal to the US supreme court. Continue reading...

item.title: Iran and US strike tankers in biggest shipping attack since war began
item.description:
Missiles launched from Iran and interceptions by Jordanian air defense systems are visible in the night sky from Damascus after Iran targeted U.S. bases in Jordan on Sept. 9, 2026. —Izz Aldien Alqasem—Getty Images Oil prices soared above $100 a barrel again Wednesday for the first time since July as the U.S. and Iran exchanged tit-for-tat strikes amid renewed hostilities. Iran targeted a U.S. base in Jordan with a series of missiles overnight, framing the assault as " retaliation for" the U.S. military destroying five Iranian oil tankers . A spokesperson for the Jordanian Armed Forces said a barrage of “20 ballistic missiles” had been launched towards its territory in the early hours. Jordan's air defense system successfully intercepted and destroyed 18 of the missiles, while the remaining two "fell in areas devoid of population centers." item.title: Seahawks pick off Patriots’ Maye three times to stage comeback in Super Bowl rematch
item.description:
Backup quarterback engineers late Seattle rally Seahawks intercept Drake Maye three times in fourth Sam Darnold exits opening drive with hip injury Backup quarterback Drew Lock led two late scoring drives and the Seattle Seahawks intercepted Drake Maye three times in the fourth quarter to overcome an early injury to starter Sam Darnold and beat the New England Patriots 13-10 on Wednesday night in a Super Bowl rematch. The Seahawks were held to just a field goal through three quarters as Lock and the offense struggled to move the ball after Darnold injured his hip on the opening drive. Continue reading...

item.title: Watch: Do Republicans blame Trump for high oil prices?
item.description:
GOP plans to center the president at rare two-day Texas event as party hopes to retain control of House in midterms Republicans are gathering in Texas on Wednesday for a rare “midterm convention”, as they attempt to convince Americans to vote for a party led by a deeply unpopular president who has overseen inflation and led the US into an increasingly unpopular war . Donald Trump will dominate the two-day convention, appearing both nights as the GOP works to cling to control of the House of Representatives in November. Republicans plan to put the president at the center of the event, a bold strategy given his approval rating is hovering at about 38%, while accusing the Democratic party of being socialist and out of touch with Americans.
